title: Gluing constructibility of $f^!K$ and restricting the adjunction
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$ and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism, in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. For $E$, use the condensed ring $S\mapsto C(S,E)$ on profinite sets, with the $\ell$-adic topology [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For $\Qlb$, use [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]: its sections on a profinite set $S$ are the continuous maps $S\to\Qlb$ whose image is contained in some finite subextension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Pull these rings back to the scheme pro-étale topoi [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and use their module-object coefficients. Use $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ and $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the full localizing closures of [sk-def-localizing-closure], and the compact-support functor $Rf_!$ with right adjoint $f^!$ supplied by [sk-prop-sf-existence].

1. Let $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ and let $X=\bigcup_{\alpha\in I}U_\alpha$ be a finite open cover with $M|_{U_\alpha}\in\Dbc(U_\alpha,\Lambda)$ for all $\alpha\in I$. Then $M\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$.
2. For $K\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$, $f^!K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$, and for $A\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ the adjunction bijection restricts naturally to
$$
\Hom_{\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)}(Rf_!A,K)\simeq\Hom_{\Dbc(X,\Lambda)}(A,f^!K).
$$

proof.text: First make the standing hypotheses explicit. The field $k$ is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to the structure maps of $X$ and $Y$. Their sources are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], so they are Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact). The rational-coefficient statement [sk-lem-coefficient-heart] identifies $\Dctf=\Dbc$ and describes constructibility as being lisse on finitely many strata. Thus $\Loc(\Dctf)=\Loc(\Dbc)$ as full subcategories by the definition [sk-def-localizing-closure]. This comparison is in the pulled-back condensed module-object categories, without replacing them by discrete field-module sheaves. The rational coefficient is the one fixed in the statement: for $\Qlb$ it is the condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], the blueprint's condensed $\Qlb$, which is also the coefficient of [sk-lem-coefficient-heart] and of the local statement used in step 4. The admissible coefficient $\Qlb$ of [sk-def-localizing-closure], and hence of the existence and coherence statements used in steps 5–6, is read as this same ring, as in the blueprint's text of that definition, whose condensed $\Qlb$ is the one just named; it is not the ring $S\mapsto C(S,\Qlb)$ of all continuous maps, which is a different condensed ring (a convergent sequence of elements of unbounded degree gives a continuous map on the one-point compactification of $\mathbf N$ that lies in no finite subextension).

source.place: Standing hypotheses implicit in both paragraphs; rational identification needed for paragraph (2).

proof.text: For (1), restriction to an open immersion is exact on coefficient modules by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Consequently it preserves kernels and images of the differentials of a representative complex, giving $\mathcal H^q(M)|_{U_\alpha}=\mathcal H^q(M|_{U_\alpha})$. If $X$ is empty, every coefficient-module sheaf is zero by the empty-cover sheaf axiom, so $M=0$ and (1) holds; this includes both an empty index set and covers consisting entirely of empty opens. Henceforth assume $X$ nonempty, so the finite index set is nonempty. Choose intervals $[a_\alpha,b_\alpha]$ with $a_\alpha\le b_\alpha$ bounding the restricted complexes, taking $[0,0]$ on an empty cover member. Put $a=\min_\alpha a_\alpha$ and $b=\max_\alpha b_\alpha$. For $q\notin[a,b]$, the sheaf $\mathcal H^q(M)$ vanishes on every cover member, hence is zero: for any pro-étale object $T\to X$, its opens $T\times_XU_\alpha$ cover it, and the sheaf axiom detects zero sections there. This proves boundedness in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

source.place: Paragraph (1), Boundedness; exactness and the empty-cover case written out.

proof.text: Continue with $X$ nonempty as in step 2. Only finitely many $q$ in $[a,b]$ can contribute. For each $\alpha$ and each such $q$, choose a finite stratification of $U_\alpha$ on which $\mathcal H^q(M|_{U_\alpha})$ is lisse, using [sk-lem-coefficient-heart]. Regard its scheme strata as immersions into $X$ by composing with $U_\alpha\hookrightarrow X$, using clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Adjoin the complement $X\setminus U_\alpha$ with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure from [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. This makes a finite scheme stratification of $X$ for each pair $(\alpha,q)$. By clause (1) of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification], these finitely many stratifications have a common finite refinement. Each nonempty refined stratum lies in some $U_\alpha$, because the opens cover $X$, and lies in one adapted stratum there for each $q$. For such an $\alpha$, the refined strata lying in $U_\alpha$ form a scheme stratification of $U_\alpha$ refining each chosen adapted stratification. Apply clause (2) of that same node to the already constructible sheaf $\mathcal H^q(M|_{U_\alpha})$ on $U_\alpha$, not to a sheaf whose global constructibility is still being proved. It is lisse on each of these refined strata, including its given scheme structure. Exact restriction from step 2 identifies this sheaf there with the restriction of $\mathcal H^q(M)$; hence every $\mathcal H^q(M)$ is lisse on the refinement. By the lisse characterization of constructibility in [sk-lem-coefficient-heart] (the strata are constructible locally closed subsets since $X$ is Noetherian, as [sk-def-sfb-constructible] notes), every $\mathcal H^q(M)$ is constructible, and the boundedness in the preceding step gives $M\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$. Empty strata are discarded; if all cohomology is zero the conclusion follows directly from the same definition.

source.place: Paragraph (1), Constructibility; finite common refinement, actual scheme strata, and lisse restriction.

proof.text: For (2), fix $K\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$. The statement [det-thm-restriction-local] supplies finitely many affine opens $u_\alpha:U_\alpha\hookrightarrow X$ covering $X$, together with affine $V_\alpha\subset Y$ and closed embeddings into affine spaces over $V_\alpha$, and it asserts $u_\alpha^*f^!K\in\Dbc(U_\alpha,\Lambda)$. Its hypotheses hold for the standing schemes and for $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$; the rational identification in step 1 puts $K$ in the domain of $f^!$. Apply (1), now proved in steps 2–3, to $M=f^!K$. This gives $f^!K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), first sentence; unit sk-thm-restriction step 2.

proof.text: Let $f=p\circ j$ be the chosen compactification in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], using the compactification convention in [sk-prop-sf-existence]. The latter specifies $j$ to be quasi-compact and $p$ proper, and defines $Rf_!$ as $Rp_*D(j_!)$ on the localizing closures. Step 1 showed $Y$ qcqs. The compactification convention [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data] cited by both nodes makes $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion. Thus [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] applies to this compactification and to the admissible rational coefficient $\Lambda$ (with $\Qlb$ read as in step 1): its composite sends $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$. Using $\Dctf=\Dbc$ from step 1 gives $Rf_!A\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$ for every $A\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), compact-support preservation; unit step 3, using the existing single-compactification component of the missing imported coherence id.

proof.text: For $A,K$ as above, use the natural Hom bijection of [sk-prop-sf-existence] on $\Loc(\Dctf)$. Steps 4–5 show that its four objects $A,f^!K,Rf_!A,K$ lie in the relevant bounded constructible subcategories. These subcategories are full in the ambient derived categories by [sk-def-sfb-constructible], as are the localizing closures by [sk-def-localizing-closure]; their Hom sets, identities and compositions on these objects are therefore exactly the same. The unchanged bijection consequently is $\Hom_{\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)}(Rf_!A,K)\simeq\Hom_{\Dbc(X,\Lambda)}(A,f^!K)$. Its naturality equations are unchanged equations of the same morphisms, so it gives the asserted restricted adjunction.

source.place: Paragraph (2), last three sentences; explicit full-subcategory Hom calculation.

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs (1)–(2), expanded with the cited existing nodes and explicit standing assumptions.
